# Guideline 2 - Your character is yours You are free to create and play whatever characters you like, as long as they fit the setting and stay believable for the station. How you portray them is up to you.
- Play as many characters as you like. You can build their lore as you go, but keep it consistent and don't rewrite it without a good reason. You can still retire a character whenever you want. - Personality, quirks, mood and outlook are entirely up to you, and they can grow over time. - Give your character flaws. Nobody is perfect, and nobody is the best at everything. Flaws that come from [textlink="their history" link="GuidelineG5"] give others something to push on, and can lead your character somewhere they normally wouldn't go. - Tie your character's background into the sector where you can: the factions, places and events that already exist in the lore. A crew with shared roots makes the world feel connected. If you want help fitting your character in, reach out to the writing team. - Within a round, keep your character coherent. A sudden change of heart is fine when there is an in-character reason for it, not just a mechanical advantage. - Carrying the same character across rounds and developing them is encouraged, but never required. - Your character remembers the shifts they survived, so let that history show: old friends, old rivals, lessons learned. See [textlink="Guideline 5" link="GuidelineG5"] for exactly what carries over.
Part of that freedom is getting into trouble. If your character is the type to start a fight in the hallway, go for it, but be ready to face the consequences in character and to [textlink="build that conflict through roleplay" link="GuidelineG3"].
